query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Nitrogen ion implantation can improve the hardness and wear resistance of TC4 alloy without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Unmodified α + β dual-phase TC4 (Ti6Al4V) alloy
generation.conditions: Ion implantation at room temperature with a fluence of 1 × 10^17 ions/cm²
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a hard TiN layer on the surface
generation.mechanism: The implanted nitrogen ions react with titanium to form a hard TiN layer, which enhances the surface hardness and wear resistance of the alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved hardness and wear resistance compared to untreated TC4 alloy
generation.boundary: Operating temperatures up to 500°C and contact stresses up to 1000 MPa
generation.uncertainty: The optimal fluence and energy of the nitrogen ions for achieving the best results are uncertain.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated TC4 alloy shows no significant improvement in wear resistance (wear rate reduction < 10%) and hardness (hardness increase < 5%) compared to the untreated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
